newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-SLANEY SHINES IN TRIUMPHANT RETURN TO MILLROSE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SLANEY SHINES IN TRIUMPHANT RETURN TO MILLROSE.

text.p: Not all the stars came out for the Millrose Games, but Mary Decker Slaney did, and shone as brightly as ever in a triumphant return to America's premier indoor track meet Friday.

Olympic headliners Jackie Joyner-Kersee and Gail Devers stayed away in a dispute with organisers over their appearance fees. Reigning 200 and 400 meter Olympic gold medallist Michael Johnson sat the event out in the television booth.
So it was left to Slaney to dazzle a sold-out Madison Square Garden with a vintage winning performance in the mile.
Accelerating in the final lap to a standing ovation, Slaney ran away from the field to win in 4 minutes 26.67 seconds, the fastest women's mile at Millrose since Paula Ivan's 4:23.72 in 1989.
Slaney, 38, holder of 11 indoor and outdoor U.S. records ranging from 800 to 3,000 meters, had not run at Millrose since finishing second to Ivan in 1989 due to a series of leg and ankle injuries.
"I was nervous because it was so long since I had been here," said Slaney, who won at Millrose in 1980, 1982-83 and 1985. "It felt so good to be back.
"This is by far the best indoor track meet in the country, there is no other place like Millrose, if you are running indoors," Slaney said.
In the meet's signature event, the Wanamaker Mile, Isaac Viciosa of Spain engineered an unexpected victory by taking the lead with two laps left to hold off Jason Pyrah of the United States.
Viciosa clocked a 3:59.34 with Pyrah finishing at 3:59.58
Defending champion Niall Bruton came in third while his Irish countryman, five-time champion Marcus O'Sullivan, finished fifth out of eight finishers.
In the women's 800 meters, Maria Mutola of Mozambique won in a blistering wire to wire performance of 2:00.39, just outside her own meet record of 2.00.23 set three years ago.
"I tried to go to the front and push the pace and see what the other girls had," said Mutola, who won in 1993-95. "If I'm leading I know I can do anything from the front."
Coming in second was defending champion Joetta Clark, who was racing in the Millrose Games for a record 19th time. Clark is a six-time meet champion and finished second for the fifth time.

Allen Johnson, the Olympic record holder in the 110-meter hurdles, failed in his attempt to break the American indoor 60-meter hurdles record of 7.36 seconds set 10 years ago by Greg Foster in edging defending champion Courtney Hawkins to win in 7.64 seconds.

Hawkins caught Johnson at the third hurdle and the pair raced side by side to the finish line before Johnson leaned in front for his second Millrose win in three years. Hawkins finished second in 7.65.
"It was so-so. I'm still a little bit rusty, it's only my first major hurdles this year," said Johnson. "A win is a win."
Said Hawkins: "I rushed the last hurdle. I want to see Allen Johnson again."

In another duel that went down to the finish line, seven-time 60 meters champion Gwen Torrence won for the third year in a row by nipping U.S. Olympic teammate Carlette Guidry-White. Torrence clocked 7.13 to Guidry-White's 7.14.
Local favourite and Olympic 400-meter hurdle champion Derrick Adkins put on a burst of speed in the last lap to run away to his second victory in the 500 meters in the last three years.
Adkins came from third to win in 1:02.98, easily ahead of seven-time meet champion Mark Everett and Andrew Valomon.
